narrative.title: The Reverse-Reading Billing Parser
narrative.scenario: A billing engine feeds expressions to a mainframe whose dialect writes operators *before* their operands (`+ a b` instead of `a + b`). The conversion desk has a trick: read the expression right-to-left, swap the parenthesis roles, and let the same precedence machinery run — then flip the assembled result to restore reading order. Implement that desk.
narrative.inputFormat: A string expression in infix form using single alphanumeric operands, the operators + - * / ^, and parentheses.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the equivalent prefix (Polish) expression as a string.
constraints: Operands are single letters or digits

testCases.explanation: The fully parenthesized input converts unambiguously; reading backwards then reversing produces the operator-first form.
Multiplication binds tighter, so the addition ends up as the outermost operator.

hintLevels: Level 1: Prefix is what you get when the postfix pipeline runs on a mirrored expression.
Level 2: Scan right-to-left, treat ')' as the opener and '(' as the closer, then reverse the output.
Level 3: Watch operator ties — with equal-precedence popping the reversed scan changes which occurrence settles first.
